title: Admin - Display Admin Permissions - Functional Test Plan
overview: Functional testing of the Admin User & Role Management - Display Admin Permissions feature on the Y4J platform. This feature displays permissions as tags under each admin card, reflecting the latest permission settings. The edge case of UI overflow when too many permissions are assigned must also be handled gracefully. Covers tag display, positioning, data accuracy, dynamic updates, and overflow behavior.

testCases.title: Permissions are displayed as tags on admin cards
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. User & Roles page is loaded with at least one admin who has permissions assigned.
steps: Observe an admin card (Limited-Access Admin with assigned permissions)
Verify the permissions section on the card
expectedResults: Permissions are displayed as individual tags/badges (not plain text list)
Each permission is a separate visual tag element
Tags are visually distinct (e.g., colored badges, rounded chips, or bordered labels)
Permission names are readable within the tags
testCases.postconditions: Permissions are confirmed displayed as tags

testCases.title: Permissions appear under each admin card
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. Multiple admin cards are displayed.
steps: Observe the first admin card - check for permissions section
Observe the second admin card - check for permissions section
expectedResults: Every admin card has a 'Permissions:' section
The permissions section is positioned below/under the admin's other details (name, email, role, status, dates)
Each card independently shows its own permissions
The permissions section is consistently positioned across all cards
testCases.postconditions: Permissions section is present under every admin card

testCases.title: Tags reflect latest permission settings - after creation
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. About to create a new admin with specific permissions.
steps: Create a new Limited-Access Admin with permissions: 'Dashboard', 'Partner Management', 'Product Management'
After creation, observe the new admin card in the list
expectedResults: The new admin card immediately shows 3 permission tags: Dashboard, Partner Management, Product Management
The tags match exactly what was selected during creation
No extra or missing permissions are shown
testCases.postconditions: Tags accurately reflect newly created permissions

testCases.title: Tags reflect latest permission settings - after edit
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. An admin with permissions 'Dashboard', 'Partner Management' exists.
steps: Find the admin card showing 'Dashboard' and 'Partner Management' tags
expectedResults: After save, the admin card shows updated tags: 'Partner Management', 'Analytics'
'Dashboard' tag is no longer displayed
'Analytics' tag is now displayed
The update is immediate without page refresh
testCases.postconditions: Tags update immediately to reflect edited permissions

testCases.title: Tags reflect latest permission settings - after role change
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. A Limited-Access Admin with partial permissions exists.
steps: Find a Limited-Access Admin card with 2-3 permission tags
Change the admin's role to 'Super Admin'
Observe the permission tags on the card
expectedResults: After role change to Super Admin, all permission tags are displayed (all 7 modules)
The tags update automatically to reflect the new full-access role
No manual permission editing is needed
testCases.postconditions: Tags reflect full permissions after role upgrade

testCases.title: Super Admin card shows all permission tags
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. A Super Admin card exists in the list.
expectedResults: Super Admin card shows all available permission tags
Tags include: Dashboard, User Management, Partner Management, Product Management, Comment Moderation, Content Management, Analytics
All 7 tags are visible
testCases.postconditions: Super Admin shows full permission set

testCases.title: Limited-Access Admin card shows only assigned permission tags
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. A Limited-Access Admin with 2 permissions exists.
expectedResults: Only the specifically assigned permissions are shown as tags
The number of tags is less than the full set (fewer than 7)
No unassigned permissions appear as tags
Tags match what was configured for this admin
testCases.postconditions: Limited-Access Admin shows correct subset of permissions

testCases.title: UI handles overflow when all permissions are assigned (many tags)
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. An admin with all 7 permissions exists (Super Admin or Limited-Access with all selected).
steps: Find an admin card with all 7 permission tags
Observe how the tags are displayed when there are many
expectedResults: All 7 permission tags are accessible (either all visible or reachable via overflow mechanism)
Tags wrap to multiple lines if needed (no horizontal overflow/clipping)
OR a 'show more' mechanism is provided if tags overflow
No tags are permanently hidden or cut off
The card layout does not break with many tags
testCases.postconditions: UI handles many tags gracefully without breaking layout

testCases.title: Permission tags have a label prefix
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. Admin cards with permissions are displayed.
steps: Observe the permissions section on any admin card
Check for a label/prefix before the tags
expectedResults: The permissions section has a 'Permissions:' label before the tags
The label clearly identifies what the tags represent
Users can understand the tags are permissions without ambiguity

testCases.title: Permission tags are consistent across page refresh
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. Admin cards with permissions are displayed.
steps: Note the permissions shown on a specific admin card
expectedResults: After refresh, the same permissions are displayed
No permissions are lost or added after refresh
Tags are loaded from the backend (not cached incorrectly)
The display is consistent and reliable
testCases.postconditions: Permission display is consistent across refreshes

testCases.title: Permission tag text matches module names exactly
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. Admin cards with permissions are displayed.
steps: Read the text of each permission tag on admin cards
Compare with the known module names in the system
expectedResults: Tag text matches the official module names (Dashboard, User Management, Partner Management, Product Management, Comment Moderation, Content Management, Analytics)
No typos or abbreviations in tag text
Tags are readable and not truncated
testCases.postconditions: Tag text is accurate and matches system module names

testCases.title: Permission tags are visible on paginated pages
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. Admin list has multiple pages.
steps: Verify permission tags on page 1 admin cards
Verify permission tags on page 2 admin cards
expectedResults: Permission tags are displayed on admin cards on all pages
Tags on page 2 are loaded correctly (not showing page 1 data)
Each admin card on every page shows its own correct permissions
testCases.postconditions: Permission tags work correctly across pagination

testCases.title: Permission tags are visible when search/filter is applied
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. Admin list is loaded.
steps: Apply a search query to filter admins
expectedResults: Permission tags remain visible on admin cards in search results
Permission tags remain visible on admin cards in filtered results
Filtering does not hide or break the permissions display
testCases.postconditions: Permission tags display correctly with search/filter active
